answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks that counterparties later verify, with each new identity starting at zero. A cedar seller and a dune buyer who collude to inflate a fresh account's reputation must lock real funds and risk losing them if disputes reveal non-delivery; repeated trades also incur fees and require distinct counterparties. This raises the cost of a sybil farm in proportion to the influence it seeks, while ivory tokens alone confer no trust.
